layer_rules.neutral: structure: text, rails, spines, outlines, gene models, single-sample signal (one ramp, hue-free)
layer_rules.identity: MAGESTIC: one colour = one molecular identity (the schematic module section 1)
layer_rules.role: RNA layer A: one colour = one argument role; data panels and signal-by-sample
layer_rules.mark: RNA layer B: splice / polya / mod marks; a mark, never a fill
layer_rules.ground: backgrounds and tints; never encodes on its own
layer_rules.rna_boundary: A colour from layer A never touches a molecular glyph; a colour from layer B never encodes a sample, a condition, a stratum or a claim. Enforced by API: tracks.gene_model / tracks.mark take no colour argument at all; panels.* take a ROLE name, not a hex.

magestic.guide: guide RNA / spacer / protospacer; the targeting half of a guide-donor
magestic.barcode: genomic barcode (bc1, N20), the landing pad and integrated barcode cassette
magestic.edit: the introduced edit itself: SNV, indel, the variant allele, the cut site
magestic.phospho: phosphothreonine (pT) marks and other post-translational recruitment marks
magestic.ink: primary linework, text, chromosome rails, plasmid backbone
magestic.rule: secondary structure: gridlines, vessel outlines, unemphasised loci
magestic.mute: recessive process arrows, step dividers, panel wash, 'other/unedited' category

rna.focal: LAYER A. The claim this manuscript makes -- the excluded register, the observed hits, the effect being argued. Never a plain category colour.
rna.reference: LAYER A. What FOCAL is measured against -- expectation under the null, the writer consensus, the reference rate, the control arm of a two-arm comparison.
rna.match: LAYER A. Sequence compatibility as an argument -- a motif that DOES fit (methylatable A, DRACH-compatible, MIG). Note the boundary: a modification MARK on a transcript glyph is layer B `mod`; 'the fraction of sites that are compatible' in a bar chart is `match`.
rna.stratum_b: LAYER A. Second stratum of that same split. Greyscale twin of stratum_a (dL* 0.8) -- panels.bars hatches it, which is the declared cue.
rna.splice: LAYER B. The splice as a molecule: 5'SS and 3'SS ticks, the branch point dot, a junction arc drawn as ANNOTATION (an arc drawn as counts per sample is a signal glyph and takes a layer-A role). Searched: worst dE 20.2 vs reference under deuteranopia; L* 23.
rna.polya: LAYER B. The 3' end as a molecule: the poly(A) / CPA / PAS site mark, a metaplot anchor line at the CPA. Searched: worst dE 21.5 vs ink under protanopia, 22.3 vs focal; L* 31. Drawn as a circle-headed lollipop so it separates from `splice` (dL* 7.3) and `mod` by form as well as hue.
rna.mod: LAYER B. An RNA modification mark (m6A, pseudouridine) on a transcript glyph, drawn as a diamond-headed lollipop. Searched: worst dE 16.6 vs match under deuteranopia (the two are related concepts -- a compatible motif and the modification on it -- so a family resemblance helps rather than misleads); L* 40.
rna.ink: 806 INK 0.15: body text on figures, exon fills, TSS arrows, rails, panel letters.
rna.hairline: 806 HAIRLINE 0.25: bar edges, axis spines, intron lines, the zero line of a mirrored track.
rna.subtle: 806 SUBTLE 0.45: provenance footer, secondary annotation, single-sample coverage fill, aligned-read blocks.
rna.neutral: 806 NEUTRAL: denominators, universes, 'not part of the argument' -- the recessive data series.
rna.mute: recessive: soft-clip blocks, dividers, 'other' categories, process arrows.
rna.wash: 806 FLOOR_BAND 0.88: 'below this is not a measurement' shading, highlighted windows, panel wash.
rna.focal_tint: 806 FOCAL_TINT: the band or fill under a FOCAL line (a CI ribbon), never a series on its own.
rna.reference_tint: 806 REFERENCE_TINT: the band or fill under a REFERENCE line.
rna.match_tint: 806 MATCH_TINT: the band or fill under a MATCH line.

semantic.rule: Encodes molecular identity. Must be mutually distinguishable under normal, deuteranopia and protanopia (dE2000 >= 12), and must reach contrast >= 2.0 on paper. Colour is the ONLY thing these carry — never use a semantic colour decoratively.

structural.rule: Carries no meaning: outlines, rails, vessel/cell outlines, recessive process arrows, step dividers. Exempt from the semantic contrast floor because being recessive is the point; still must not be mistaken for a semantic colour it sits beside.

semantic.rule: Encodes an argument role (layer A) or a molecular identity (layer B). All nine must be mutually distinguishable under normal, deuteranopia and protanopia (dE2000 >= 12) and reach contrast >= 2.0 on paper. A pair between declarable_min_delta_e and 12 may be admitted ONLY with a named form cue in `cvd_redundancy`; below declarable_min_delta_e a declaration is refused and the hex must change (that is how `control` was replaced).

magestic.units: thin space before unit; use 'bp', 'kb', 'nt' roman

rna.panel_letter: bold lowercase a, b, c at the top-left of the axes (the figure standard owns this)
rna.gene_names: italic for gene names in every organism (PDH1, TMEM41B); roman for proteins (Rna15, Ysh1) and for RNA species (mRNA, snRNA)
rna.coordinates: chrXVI:558,219-560,137 with thousands separators; kb on a browser axis; 5' -> 3' left to right, so a minus-strand locus is drawn on a REVERSED x-axis
rna.units: thin space before unit; 'nt' for RNA lengths, 'bp' for genomic, 'kb' on axes
rna.primes: use U+2032 (′) for 5′ and 3′, never an apostrophe

callout.note: Detail is QUARANTINED in a dashed callout box (Levy 2015 / Findlay 2018 device), never inlined into the overview.

process_arrow.note: Process arrows are RECESSIVE and neutral. They must never compete with semantic colour. Prefer a verb-labelled divider rule over an arrow where the step is sequential rather than molecular.

declared_cues.cue: barcode is always drawn as rungs (the identity motif); focal is a data fill or a diamond marker

magestic.$schema_note: MAGESTIC figure design tokens. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for palette, type and geometry. Every renderer (SVG glyph library, matplotlib theme, slide theme) reads this file. Do not hard-code a colour anywhere else.
magestic.provenance: Palette derived from the Okabe-Ito colour-vision-deficiency-safe set as published in Wong, B. 'Points of view: Color blindness', Nature Methods 8, 441 (2011), doi:10.1038/nmeth.1618 (figure viewed and values transcribed directly from its table). Deviations from Okabe-Ito are documented per-token in `note`. Structural neutrals are original. Validated by tests/palette_check.py.

callout.note: Detail is QUARANTINED in a dashed callout box (Levy 2015 / Findlay 2018 device), never inlined into the overview.

process_arrow.note: Process arrows are RECESSIVE and neutral. They must never compete with semantic colour. Prefer a verb-labelled divider rule over an arrow where the step is sequential rather than molecular.

principles.1_one_reading_path: Each panel has exactly one unambiguous reading order. Lanes read build -> grow -> read.
principles.2_steps_are_typography: Sequential steps are verb-labelled divider rules, not arrow thickets. Arrows are reserved for genuine molecular transitions.
principles.3_multiplicity_not_detail: Pooled complexity is shown by many small flat coloured blobs, not by one elaborately rendered cell.
principles.4_quarantine_detail: Mechanism detail lives in a dashed callout box tied to the overview by leaders.
principles.5_colour_is_identity: Colour encodes molecular identity and nothing else, and must vary in LIGHTNESS as well as hue (Wong 2011). Structure stays neutral.
principles.6_rank_visual_weight: Three stroke tiers and a 2-neutral + <=4-accent budget per panel, so unimportant things actually recede.
principles.7_propagate_identity: A colour assigned to an entity follows it through every stage of the experiment (Findlay 2018).

identity.note: A literal black-and-white barcode forming the base-pair rungs of a duplex. Scientifically honest (the barcode really is written into the genome) and visually distinctive. Use as the project mark on title slides, dividers, posters and preprint banners, and as the flat-vector `barcode` glyph in figures. The photoreal 3D treatment of the cover does NOT survive greyscale or small sizes and must not become the manuscript language.

A.name: argument roles
A.contract: One colour = one ARGUMENT ROLE across the whole manuscript. FOCAL is never a plain category colour; if two series are strata of one measurement they take stratum_a / stratum_b and FOCAL stays free for the annotation that carries the point. REFERENCE is never used for a second focal series. Greys carry everything the argument does not turn on.
applies_to: signal glyphs coloured by SAMPLE: coverage fills, junction arcs, read pileups, 3'-end profiles

B.name: molecular identities
B.contract: One colour = one MOLECULAR IDENTITY, forever, in every figure of both labs. Neutral-first: the gene model (exon, UTR, intron), reads and single-sample coverage are drawn in the structural greys -- structure is never coloured. Hue is spent on three MARKS only, and a B accent is a mark (tick, arc, lollipop), never a fill.

neutral_glyphs.utr: ink fill at utr_height_ratio of the exon height (form carries the distinction, not colour)
neutral_glyphs.intron: hairline stroke in `hairline` grey, optional chevrons in the direction of transcription
neutral_glyphs.tss: bent arrow in ink at the 5' end
neutral_glyphs.read: `subtle` fill for an aligned block; soft-clip = `mute` fill with hatch; junction gap = hairline
neutral_glyphs.read_tail: the A-rich poly(A) PREFIX of a read's 3' clip is a `polya` fill on that read -- ONE hue for the 3' end, its site mark and its tail (rbrowse paints tails base-A green on screen; the publication path keeps one identity per hue). A 1-px ink rule at the body/tail junction is the form cue (rbrowse finding [9]: that boundary is the most-read edge in the tool and a rule survives any palette)
neutral_glyphs.read_clip: the non-A remainder of a soft clip is `mute` -- unaligned, not poly(A)
neutral_glyphs.compressed_reads: a merged raster (per-column MAJORITY) or a ribbon wedge (per-column FRACTION as height) -- rbrowse's representations, ported to rectify.visualize.pileup; the body is `subtle` or the sample's layer-A role

applies_to: compressed read views (merged raster, ribbon wedge)
union-exon (spliced) axis and isoform chain rows
junction arcs as counts (signal) or annotation

layers.cross_layer_separation: MEASURED 2026-09-05: every B mark clears every A role at dE2000 >= 16.6 in normal, deuteranopia and protanopia (worst: match vs mod, deuteranopia). Five of the six A fills sit >= 17 L* LIGHTER than every B mark (A fills L* 46-71; B marks L* 23-40); the plum `control` (L* 35) is the exception and clears the marks by hue (>= 14.4) and by form instead. B marks share hue FAMILIES with A (a dark red beside vermillion, an indigo beside blue, a forest green beside green) because seven Okabe-Ito hues already occupy the hue circle; hue distance, lightness and form (mark vs fill) together are what stop a reader linking them -- DESIGN.md section 2 says why that is enough.

principles.1_two_layers: Argument roles on data panels; molecular identities on glyphs; never cross (layers.boundary_rule).
principles.2_structure_is_grey: Gene models, reads and single-sample signal are drawn in the grey ramp. Hue is spent on the three marks and on the argument.
principles.4_form_is_the_second_channel: Every distinction that encodes something survives a mono printout: hatch for stratum_b, shape for the three marks, annotation-not-fill for focal beside strata.
principles.5_five_to_three: A locus is read 5' -> 3' left to right; a minus-strand locus reverses the x-axis rather than mirroring the reader.
principles.6_signal_is_data: Coverage, arcs-as-counts and pileups belong to a SAMPLE and are coloured by the argument; annotation belongs to the molecule.
principles.7_rank_visual_weight: Three stroke tiers and a 2-neutral + <= 4-accent budget per panel.
